task_specification.objective: Replace visible enemy scaffolding with cohesive authored role presentations, bind a compatible Warden animation package through an explicit seven-state profile, and deliver distinct event-owned audio for all three weapon families so Tester can qualify ordinary play, dense final-wave combat, failure, victory, result, and clean replay as one release-ready run.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by three concrete presentation integrations: ordinary enemies are still constructed from runtime PrimitiveMesh parts; the Warden animation adapter relies on clip-name inference while its bound package cannot supply seven distinct semantic clips; and all three weapon arrays are intentionally empty after unsuitable auditions, so valid attack transactions produce audio rejections. These defects prevent the otherwise implemented run lifecycle from meeting the coherent-art, semantic-feedback, and complete-run release contracts.

stop_conditions: Do not modify, replace, duplicate, or restructure the intact authored cemetery package, its sightline camera behavior, or its native landmarks.
Do not weaken truthful animation or audio validation, map unrelated clips to missing semantics, or count generic tones and unsuitable firearm-derived auditions as accepted Mournlight feedback.
Do not alter the preserved automatic-combat transaction rules, deterministic targeting, hit policies, encounter retirement order, or title/pause/result input ownership.

If no compatible, licensable production asset can satisfy an assigned family after bounded audition and runtime inspection, stop that task with the exact incompatibility recorded instead of shipping a placeholder.
Do not claim complete-run or issue closure from Developer self-validation; formal recapture, audio judgment, performance qualification, and closure remain with GameLoop Runtime and Tester.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause treatment from prior transform and procedural-presentation work: replace runtime primitive construction with direct authored instances, replace animation token guessing with an explicit compatible-package profile, and replace deliberately empty weapon-audio bindings with accepted event-owned sources. Preserve the working cemetery, combat, lifecycle, camera, and retirement systems around these narrow repairs.

code: Run the pinned native Godot project and host boot checks; require successful resource import, clean parsing, clean editor errors, and no runtime debugger errors.

Inspect shipped scene/resource bindings to confirm ordinary enemy presenters no longer instantiate PrimitiveMesh scaffolding and every new external runtime asset has matching provenance and notice coverage.
Assert the Warden profile contains seven distinct valid mappings and the audio library contains non-empty family onset/impact arrays with explicit owners, priorities, volumes, and bounded limits.
Regression-check combat, encounter retirement, input routing, release-only guards, and Retry reset code so the preserved transaction and lifecycle invariants remain unchanged.
runtime: Tester should replay ordinary movement and dense final-profile combat, requiring all four enemy roles, Bellkeeper, seven Warden animation states, three weapon identities, causal counts, zero missing semantic dispatches, and clean pool/retry resets.

Tester should execute the complete seven-to-ten-minute title-to-victory route plus natural failure, result, Retry, and Return to Title, confirming five waves, upgrades, boss phases, statistics, build summary, credits/provenance, and no stale actors or audio.

Capture mixed-output audio analysis for isolated Lantern, Gravespade, and Wisps events and for dense combat, checking recognizable bounded onsets/impacts, priority audibility, voice limits, and absence of generic tones, firearm reports, speech, hum, or leaks.
Preserve the existing final-wave density/performance instrumentation for later native 1920x1080 qualification; do not treat the llvmpipe 1280x720 sample as representative hardware evidence.
